data.title: P. Schreiber: Early medieval occupation of the Marikovská valley region
data.excerpt: A short but all the more interesting article by Peter Schreiber, archaeologist of the Trenčín Museum, on the Slavic occupation of the Marikovská valley. Four early medieval sites are known in the area, dated between the 7th and the 10th century, and the most important of them, Dolná Mariková – Šimúnky, yielded finds that point to a magnate class of warriors.

children.text: We bring you a short but all the more interesting article by Mgr. Peter Schreiber on the Slavic occupation of the Marikovská valley. The author is an archaeologist of the Trenčín Museum.

In the area of the Marikovská valley there are four sites dated to the period of the Early Middle Ages. The chronological placing of the sites falls from the 7th to the 10th century. Almost all the sites are already known and published in the literature.

with its finds broadly dated to the 7th to 9th centuries, (Fig. 1: 1, 2; Map 1: 1), (Budinský-Krička 1950). On the south-eastern edge of the defined area lies the site of Jasenica/Považské Podhradie, the locality known as Hradište. This is a hilltop position with finds of an iron ploughshare and a riding spur, dated to the 8th to 9th (?) century
, (Fig. 2: 1, 2; Map 1: 2). The third site is Hatné, the locality known as Záhradčie, with its finds dated to the 9th century (Map 1: 3; Petrovský-Šichman 1964).

children.text: The fourth and most important site is Dolná Mariková, Šimúnky, the locality known as Široká (Map 1: 4). This is a hilltop settlement with occupation from several periods

. The concentration of finds of the Early Middle Ages at Šimúnky – Široká lies on a relatively small acropolis, which is naturally protected on the northern to north-western side by inaccessible rock faces (Figs 3, 4). From the southern to south-eastern side the position was the most accessible
. The finds themselves point to a magnate class of warriors

. The concentration of these finds on the rocky acropolis could in turn demonstrate a sudden demise of this place in the course of the Early Middle Ages. It would be possible to determine the likely time of the demise of the occupation on the basis of a closer analysis of the metal objects, the equipment and the armament. It could have been an internal tribal conflict in the course of the 9th century, or the destruction of the settlement in the period around the 10th century in connection with the campaigns of the Ugrian tribes, or with the formation of the newly emerging Hungarian state in the 11th century.

children.text: A stray find of a finger ring comes from the cadastral area of the village of Horná Mariková, the hamlet of Hapovce. On the basis of analogies from the cemeteries at Čakajovce and Krásno we can date the find of the finger ring from Horná Mariková only very broadly, from the end of the 10th to the first half of the 15th century.

The mountain ridges of the Púchov Upland and of the low Javorníky, as well as the saddle between the villages of Hoštiná and Klieština, created the preconditions for communication routes between the valley of the Biela voda and the Marikovská valley. In this context the old mountain road which, according to tradition, ran between the town of Púchov and the valley of Mariková may also be of interest. In the wider area of the town of Púchov, significant finds of the Early Middle Ages come from the locality designated as “hydináreň” (the poultry farm), dated to the first half of the 9th century (Bialeková 1977). A more extensive Slavic settlement was probably situated in that locality
(Fig. 5: 1, 2; Map 1: 7). Two further sites within the town of Púchov, dated from the 7th to the 10th century, lie close to the floodplain of the Váh, within the built-up area of the town

(Map 1: 8, 9). It is precisely the sites in the area of the town of Púchov, which lie on the right bank of the river Váh, that could have had a direct connection with the occupation in the submontane to mountain area of the Marikovská valley during the Early Middle Ages.
